1.explanation:
• src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js defines the core comment rules (including block comments) for all ECMAScript-family languages. Our empty-comment edge case lives here.
• src/languages/javascript.js imports and configures that ECMA grammar specifically for plain JavaScript.
• src/languages/typescript.js does the same for TypeScript (which re-uses the block/comment modes from ecmascript.js).

All three files participate in recognizing and ending `/*…*/`-style comments. Because the bug manifests whenever an immediately closed block comment appears, you have to revise the comment mode in ecmascript.js and ensure both its JavaScript and TypeScript wrappers honor the fixed behavior.
1.bug_scenario: When you sprinkle empty block comments (/**/) around JavaScript code — for example `/**/console.log("Hello, World!")/**/` — the highlighter recognizes the first empty comment, highlights the `console.log` call correctly, then eats the trailing empty comment and never switches back into JavaScript mode. Everything after that point appears un­styled. In other words, an empty `/* … */` comment resets the parser state but doesn’t restore the JS mode, so the rest of the line (and any following code) is left plain.

2.explanation:
• src/languages/javascript.js: This file defines the JavaScript grammar and explicitly includes the C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE (the rule that matches /**…*/). The empty comment case manifests here.  
• src/languages/typescript.js: TypeScript reuses the JavaScript comment rules (and extends them), so it is equally affected by an empty /**/ block.  
• src/lib/mode_compiler.js: This module contains the core COMMENT helper (COMMENT(begin,end,options)) and compiles the begin/end regexes. Handling of zero-length block comments is implemented here; a fix is required so that an empty ‘/*…*/’ still advances the parser without breaking the highlight stream.
2.bug_scenario: An empty JavaScript block-comment “/**/” at the start (or end) of a snippet causes Highlight.js’s JavaScript/TypeScript grammar to stop tokenizing further code. In the first screenshot the leading “/**/” is parsed as an empty comment, but the very next “console.log(…)” and the trailing “/**/” are left un-highlighted. The expected behavior is that both console.log and the trailing comment should be highlighted normally.
